page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, providing a standard compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include basic AVX, AES, and SHA_NI acceleration flags, while advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX are not present.

Hardware bundling on this instance excludes both dedicated GPUs and local disk storage, requiring all persistent root disks and data volumes to be attached externally via network block storage. Network performance is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier performance across general computational tasks. PassMark CPU testing yields an average score of 10,249.39, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations record scores of 1,315.0 and 5,025.0 respectively. While synthetic stress-ng benchmarks show weaker throughput under extreme CPU and memory load, real-world utility remains solid. Memory read throughput reaches 395.92 GB/sec in cached operations, and application-level metrics demonstrate capable throughput, including 7.44 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.78 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation delivers cost-efficient compute capacity for organizations running processing pipelines that do not require expansive in-memory state. Due to the lack of onboard storage and modest baseline network throughput, this instance is best suited for compute tasks like continuous integration agents, application servers, microservices, batch processing, and standard web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor at 2.6 GHz. Delivering an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio. It operates under the KVM hypervisor without local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic testing reflects moderate multi-core compute capability, with a PassMark CPU score of 10,249.39 and Geekbench multi-core mark of 5,025.0. Application metrics show stable mid-range throughput, generating 7.44 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.78 GB/sec in static web server testing. The server provides a cost-effective environment for compute-bound tasks, making it suitable for distributed build jobs, microservices, batch compute workloads, and general web application hosting.
